frameworks.name: Whisper-Tease-Shout Launch Sequence
frameworks.definition: A three-phase promotional cadence for any product launch: Whisper (6+ weeks out, build anticipation with no details), Tease (6 weeks to 7 days out, reveal partial content), Shout (final 7 days, direct reminders). Each phase has distinct content strategy and contact frequency.

frameworks.name: Two-Tier Affiliate Architecture
frameworks.definition: A structure distinguishing super-affiliates (large audiences, status-motivated, rewarded with scarce-access prizes tied to audience benefit) from regular affiliates (small audiences, rewarded with low-bar achievable bonuses). Incentive design differs for each tier.

frameworks.name: Triple Aligned Incentive Test
frameworks.definition: A validation gate for any affiliate promotion: the affiliate's incentive, the creator's incentive, and the audience's incentive must all point toward the same action (the click or signup). Any misalignment reduces outcome.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi structured his $100M Leads book launch affiliate program so that super-affiliates were rewarded with a live Q&A session for their audience rather than a personal cash prize, because framing the prize as an audience benefit rather than a personal reward converts affiliate promotional emails from audience withdrawals into audience goodwill deposits.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: High-status affiliates with large, loyal audiences
Creator (Alex Hormozi) has scarce public availability as a credible signal
claims.mechanism: Affiliates can legitimately tell their audience 'click my link so our community wins access,' converting the ask from a withdrawal to a gift; audience incentive aligns with affiliate incentive and creator incentive, amplifying promotion depth.
bounded_by: Does not apply when the creator is ubiquitously available — scarcity signal must be genuine
Does not apply when affiliate audience has no prior trust in the creator

claims.text: For affiliate program design, the more incentive tiers are aligned (affiliate's incentive + creator's incentive + audience's incentive all pointing to the same action), the larger the promotional outcome. Alex Hormozi argues that paying affiliates financially aligns only two of the three incentives, leaving audience incentive unaddressed, which limits effectiveness.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Affiliate model where audience trust is a scarce asset
Applies to B2C and event/book launches; B2B may weigh financial incentive differently
claims.mechanism: Audiences see through promotions that benefit only the affiliate financially; adding audience-direct benefit removes the perception of self-interest and increases engagement with the affiliate's promotional message.
bounded_by: Pure financial affiliate models still work for commodity products where audience trust in the affiliate is lower

claims.text: Affiliate programs should have two polar-opposite tiers: a high-bar competitive tier (e.g., top 10 wins scarce access) to capture status-driven super-affiliates, and a low-bar achievable tier (e.g., get 10 attendees) to prevent small-list holders from opting out of promotion entirely. Running only a competitive top tier causes small-list affiliates to self-exclude.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Affiliate programs with a heterogeneous size distribution of affiliates

numbers.axis: Affiliate list-size tier vs. prize structure

anchors.value: Top 10 get live AMA with creator for their audience
Anyone sending 10+ attendees gets two bonus chapters

bounded_by: Does not apply when the product category is commodity and financial payout is the primary affiliate motivator

claims.text: Recruiting affiliates by cause-alignment rather than financial incentive produces missionaries (committed, sustained promotion) rather than mercenaries (short-term, highest-bidder promotion). Mercenary affiliates trigger a race to the top in payout rates, making the channel economically unsustainable for the business owner.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Creator/brand with genuine goodwill and track record of over-delivery
Product category where audience trust is central (books, events, coaching)
claims.mechanism: Cause-aligned affiliates promote authentically and persistently; financially-motivated affiliates switch to the next highest payer, causing churn in the channel and escalating commission costs.
bounded_by: In commodity or B2B product categories with no strong creator brand, financial incentive is the primary driver and this distinction is less actionable

claims.text: Affiliate opt-in friction should be calibrated to the product price point: low friction (30-second form, no tax paperwork) maximizes volume for low-price B2C products; higher friction (1099 tax forms, qualification steps) filters for quality and intent in B2B or high-ticket service contexts.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: B2C low-price product (e.g., a book): maximize volume, minimize friction
B2B or high-ticket service: qualify affiliates and their audiences before granting access
claims.mechanism: Friction acts as a self-selection filter; affiliates who complete friction steps are more committed to promoting. For low-ticket items this filter is unnecessary because volume outweighs quality.

numbers.axis: Affiliate sign-up friction vs. product type

anchors.value: 30-second form (first name, last name, email, phone), no tax documentation
1099/K-1 tax form required, qualification questions added

claims.text: Small UX changes in an affiliate opt-in flow can produce large changes in affiliate signup volume. Alex Hormozi reported that changing the banner at the top of the affiliate opt-in form increased affiliate signups by 60%, and adding a copy of the custom affiliate link in an automated email (versus only displaying it on the thank-you page) drove a roughly 25% increase in the number of affiliates who actively promoted.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Affiliate opt-in page for a book launch event (2023, $100M Leads launch)

numbers.axis: UX change vs. affiliate activation impact

anchors.region: Banner copy change on opt-in form
Adding link copy to follow-up email vs. thank-you page only

bounded_by: Single campaign data point; generalizability to other affiliate products not confirmed by Hormozi

claims.text: During a product launch, affiliates should be messaged at most two to three times over the full campaign duration to become affiliates, because over-messaging customers (who make up the majority of the list) erodes goodwill faster than it gains promotional lift.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Sending affiliate recruitment messages to a mixed list of customers and prospective affiliates
claims.mechanism: Most readers on a customer list are buyers, not promoters; treating them repeatedly as potential affiliates makes the sender appear transactional and depletes the trust balance built through value content.

numbers.axis: Maximum affiliate recruitment emails to customer list over campaign duration

anchors.value: 6+ weeks of repeated affiliate recruitment emails, causing audience fatigue before the event

bounded_by: Once a customer opts in as an affiliate, they have consented to more frequent contact (weekly update emails, etc.)

claims.text: Once affiliates are recruited, the hardest part is getting them to advertise consistently rather than once. Sustained affiliate promotion requires proactive re-engagement: periodic content refreshes (to prevent ad creative fatigue), regular scoreboard updates (showing each affiliate their rank and lead count), and small engagement tokens.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Multi-week affiliate campaign where affiliates are not financially paid per conversion

claims.text: In a Whisper-Tease-Shout launch, the effectiveness of the Shout phase (final 7 days) is primarily determined by how much goodwill and value the creator provided before that phase. Creators who skip the Whisper and Tease phases must artificially manufacture value and frequency simultaneously, which reads as disjointed and burns audience trust without generating proportional response.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Creator or brand with an existing audience that has a goodwill balance
Product or event launch with a defined date
claims.mechanism: Audience goodwill (accumulated by prior value delivery) is the underlying asset being drawn on during Shout; without it, the Shout is a cold ask that triggers skepticism rather than urgency.

anchors.value: 6+ weeks before launch: drip minimal anticipation signals, no content details
6 weeks to 7 days before: reveal partial content, trailers, excerpts
Final 7 days: direct reminders, 'be there' messaging, high frequency

bounded_by: Requires a pre-existing audience with goodwill; does not apply to cold-launch situations with no prior relationship

claims.text: During a promotional campaign, base content volume (value delivery on core topics) should not decrease even as launch content is added on top. Adding promotional content while reducing base value content is self-defeating because it signals to the audience that the creator is now prioritizing their own goals over the audience's interests.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Creator with an established regular content cadence launching a product or event

claims.text: Affiliate programs create an elevated quality standard for the creator's own messaging and advertising because affiliates — who are risking their own audience's trust — will demand higher standards than the creator would hold themselves to. Alex Hormozi made last-minute tweaks to book launch messaging only after close affiliates flagged gaps, tweaks he would not have made otherwise.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Affiliates are trusted peers or close contacts who know the creator's offer well

claims.text: For brick-and-mortar service businesses (e.g., massage), an affiliate strategy targeting local employers — offering employees free service as part of new-hire onboarding packets — requires no financial incentive to the employer because the employer's benefit (being perceived as a more caring employer) is distinct from and non-competing with the service provider's benefit (new customers).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Local brick-and-mortar service business (massage, physical therapy, similar)
Target employer hires regularly and values retention/onboarding quality
Service provider can absorb cost of free sessions as a customer-acquisition expense
claims.mechanism: Employer and service provider are not competitors; both parties gain independently, removing the negotiation framing entirely. No financial payment needed because the offer is pure benefit to the employer at near-zero cost.
bounded_by: Does not apply when the service provider and employer are in competing or overlapping categories
Requires volume of employers to fill meaningful calendar capacity

claims.text: Alex Hormozi sent two affiliate recruitment emails to his existing customer/follower list for the $100M Leads book launch and generated 9,000 affiliate sign-ups, the majority of whom subsequently promoted the event to their own audiences.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Creator with large, high-goodwill email list built over years
Product (book event) with no financial incentive to affiliates — goodwill-driven
2023 $100M Leads launch

numbers.axis: Affiliate recruitment email volume vs. affiliate sign-ups

bounded_by: Hormozi's existing goodwill level with his list is not representative of a creator with limited track record

claims.text: Well-designed promotional advertisements should themselves be valuable and shareable — analogous to movie trailers — so that the audience shares them organically, increasing reach without additional paid spend. The value embedded in the advertisement is both an ethical requirement and a distribution multiplier.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Content-based businesses or creators with educationally-oriented audiences
claims.mechanism: Audiences share content they find useful; if the ad is valuable in itself, the share is motivated by positive social identity signaling rather than product endorsement — organic distribution that doesn't deplete goodwill.
bounded_by: Applies primarily to education and event-based products; less applicable to pure transactional or commodity advertising

claims.text: Showing proof of long creative investment in a product (e.g., documenting two years of writing) dramatically increases the perceived value of the final product relative to the same product framed as a short-duration effort. This is because elapsed work time serves as a quality signal even when the audience cannot evaluate the content directly.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Products where quality is difficult to evaluate before purchase (books, courses, events)
claims.mechanism: Effort duration signals commitment and therefore quality; audiences infer that a creator who invested years would not deliver poor output, reducing purchase risk perception.
bounded_by: Does not apply to commodity products where quality is directly observable pre-purchase

claims.text: Alex Hormozi sent content emails to confirmed affiliates at a rate of two per week for the five-week pre-launch period, and communicated this frequency commitment upfront so affiliates could calibrate expectations. Keeping stated communication commitments to affiliates is a trust-building prerequisite for sustained affiliate promotion.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Multi-week affiliate campaign with non-financially-compensated affiliates

numbers.axis: Affiliate communication cadence over pre-launch period

examples.text: Alex Hormozi used the $100M Leads book launch as a live demonstration of the affiliate strategy described in the book itself. He recruited affiliates via a 30-second opt-in form at acquisition.com/affiliate, offered the top 10 affiliates a live Q&A with their audience and two bonus chapters to anyone who drove 10+ attendees, sent two emails to his customer list generating 9,000 affiliate signups, and maintained a two-email-per-week affiliate communication cadence with content refreshes mid-campaign to prevent ad fatigue. He reported that a banner change on the opt-in page lifted affiliate signups 60% and that adding a link copy in the follow-up email increased active promoters by roughly 25%.

A massage therapist implementing a local affiliate strategy approaches a nearby chiropractor and offers free massages to any patient whose back has just been adjusted. The chiropractor — who sees 50 new patients a month — begins referring a percentage of those patients. No financial payment is exchanged initially; the referral relationship is maintained by the massage therapist also sending patients to the chiropractor, creating a mutual reciprocity loop that sustains the channel. Adding financial incentives on top of this relationship is optional and can further accelerate volume.

Alex Hormozi used the Godzilla movie teaser as an analogy for the Whisper phase: the teaser shows only a foot, no plot, no characters, just a release date. It creates anticipation without any content reveal. Over the two years before the $100M Leads launch, Hormozi dripped small signals — 'another day of writing,' 'something good coming' — without revealing any contents, building curiosity that made the eventual release feel significant.

practices.text: When designing an affiliate program, identify both an affiliate avatar (what motivates the affiliate) and a customer avatar (what the affiliate's audience wants). Build separate offers for each and ensure both are satisfied by the promotion.
Provide affiliates with new content assets (scripts, graphics, talking points) at the midpoint of a campaign to prevent their promotional creative from going stale with their audience.
After the campaign ends, announce winners publicly and deliver the prizes that were promised exactly as specified. Prize delivery is a trust signal for future affiliate campaigns.

Treat affiliated audiences with the same or higher messaging care as your own audience — never send communications to the affiliate-referred audience that reveal that your primary goal is financial. Frame all communications around the value the audience will receive.
Provide affiliates with their real-time ranking and lead count via regular email updates during the campaign. Affiliates who cannot see their standing disengage faster.
When launching a product via affiliates, maintain your baseline content output at its normal volume and add affiliate promotional content on top of — not instead of — it.
